privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how personal data is processed based on how Pétanque Analytics currently works. It does not guarantee full legal compliance.

s1.title: 1. Service identity
s1.p1: Pétanque Analytics is an app for managing and analysing pétanque statistics (matches, training, precision shooting). It is available on the web (petanque-analytics.com) and on Android.

s2.title: 2. Purpose of processing
s2.intro: Data is processed to provide the service, including:
items: creating and authenticating a user account;
verifying the email address and enabling password reset;
recording players, matches, training sessions and shooting sessions linked to the account;
calculating and displaying statistics from entered game actions.
s2.outro: This processing is necessary to provide the service you request. The app is not monetised today: no advertising is integrated and no payment data is collected.

s3.title: 3. Personal data collected
accountItems: password (stored only as a hash, never returned by the API);
s3.playerTitle: Player profile (if you create or link a player)
playerItems: a “club” column exists in the database but is not offered in the current interface.
s3.gameTitle: Game data linked to the player
gameItems: matches: format, target score, statistics mode, team names, nature, competition, terrain type, comment, participants, ends, roles, balls (score, point/shot type, optional distance);
training sessions (point or shot): distance, number of balls, attempts, scores, dates;
precision shooting sessions: 20 shots, scores, optional title / description / context nature.
s3.statsNote: Displayed statistics are not stored separately: they are calculated on read from recorded actions.
authItems: session token (JWT) issued by the API, kept on the device in browser or app local storage, for about 14 days;
one-time tokens (hashed) for email verification (valid 24 hours) and password reset (valid 1 hour).
deviceItems: match or shooting session drafts not yet sent to the server.
s3.notCollected: The app does not collect in its current code: phone number, profile photo, advertising ID, contacts, GPS location, payment data, or health data.

s4.title: 4. Providers and hosting
s4.p1: Business data is stored on the application infrastructure (API https://api.petanque-analytics.com, MySQL on the same virtual server, not publicly exposed). The site is served over HTTPS via Caddy (Let’s Encrypt certificates).
s4.hosting: Hosting: virtual server (VPS) at Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany.
s4.resend: Transactional emails (address confirmation, password reset) are sent via Resend. Resend receives the recipient email address and message content (one-time link). No marketing emails are sent by the app in its current state.
s4.googlePlay: If the app is installed from Google Play, Google may process data related to app distribution, outside the scope of Pétanque Analytics code.
s4.noTracking: The app does not include audience analytics, crash reporting, or advertising kits (no Google Analytics, Firebase Analytics, Sentry, or equivalent in the code).

s5.title: 5. Cookies
s5.p1: The web frontend does not use tracking or advertising cookies. Authentication relies on a locally stored token (localStorage), not a session cookie.

s6.title: 6. Technical logs
s6.p1: Like any web service, the reverse proxy (Caddy) may record technical logs (e.g. IP address, date, requested URL) for operation and security. The API may log an internal user identifier if email sending fails. A rate limiter uses the IP address and a hash of the email to limit abuse (forgot password, resend verification email). Retention of these infrastructure logs is not defined in the application code.

s7.title: 7. No advertising or sale of data
s7.p1: In the current code, the app contains no advertising. Personal data is not sold.

s8.title: 8. Retention
s8.p1: Account and game data remain while the account exists. After account deletion (see below), the email, hashed password, and authentication tokens linked to the account are removed. Verification and reset tokens expire according to the durations above if not used.

s9.title: 9. Account deletion and retained data
s9.p1: You can delete your account from the app (Settings) or from the {link} after signing in.
deletedItems: the account (email, password, verification date) is removed;
verification and reset tokens linked to the account are removed;
the session token becomes invalid; the app signs you out.
s9.kept: The player profile (first name, last name, nickname) is not destroyed: the link to the account is removed. Matches, training and shooting sessions linked to that player are kept. This preserves match history involving other players. The “created by” link on a match to the account is removed.
s9.extended: If you want broader deletion of game data still associated with your name, you can request it at the contact address above. Such a request may affect history visible to other users.

s10.title: 10. Your rights
s10.intro: Under applicable law (including the GDPR if you are in the European Economic Area), you may have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and, where applicable, portability.
items: player profile rectification: Account settings, once signed in;
account erasure: delete account, subject to the limits described above;
other requests: by email to the contact address below.

s11.title: 11. Security
s11.p1: Communication between the app and the API uses HTTPS. Passwords are hashed. This reduces certain risks but does not guarantee zero incidents.

s12.title: 12. Changes
s12.p1: This policy may be updated to reflect service changes. The date at the top of the page is the last update of the text published in the app.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms of use govern access to Pétanque Analytics. By creating an account or using the service, you accept these terms.

s1.title: 1. Purpose of the service
s1.p1: Pétanque Analytics is a free service for tracking and analysing pétanque statistics. It lets you record matches, training sessions and precision shooting sessions, and view statistics calculated from those entries.
s1.p2: The service is provided “as is”. It is not an official competition tool and does not guarantee sporting accuracy, absence of input errors, or any particular outcome.

s2.title: 2. Access conditions
s2.p1: Main features require creating an account with an email address and password. Internet access is required. The Android app and website use the same API.
s2.p2: You must provide a valid email address. A verification email is sent. Some features may remain usable before confirmation; you should confirm your address when asked.

s3.title: 3. Account and security
s3.p1: You are responsible for keeping your credentials confidential and for use of your account. If you think a third party has access, change your password via “forgot password”.
s3.p2: The password must meet the minimum length required at registration. It is stored as a hash. A session token is kept on your device; signing out removes it locally without deleting the account.

s4.title: 4. Use of the service
s4.intro: You agree to use the service normally and lawfully, including:
items: not knowingly entering unlawful content in free fields (comments, names, etc.);
not attempting to disrupt, overload, or bypass the service, its technical limits, or its security;
not accessing another account’s data or attempting to do so.
s4.outro: Players, clubs (if ever recorded), and statistics you enter are your responsibility. You must have the necessary information to record them, especially for third parties.

s5.title: 5. Data you provide
s5.p1: You remain the owner of information you enter. You authorise the publisher to host and process it only to provide, maintain, and secure the service, in line with the {privacy}.
s5.p2: You may delete your account at any time. Effects on game data (player profile kept in match history) are described in the {privacy}.
s5.p3: Details are also available on the {delete} page.

s6.title: 6. Intellectual property
s6.p1: The app, its name, interface, and code are protected. You may not copy, extract, or reuse the service beyond personal use, except with permission or as allowed by law.

s7.title: 7. Availability, maintenance, and changes
s7.p1: The publisher strives to keep the service available but cannot guarantee uninterrupted access. Outages may occur (maintenance, incident, evolution, hosting constraints).
s7.p2: Features may be added, changed, or removed. As the service is free and evolving, changes may occur without notice, within reason.

s8.title: 8. Suspension or deletion for abuse
s8.p1: In case of abusive, fraudulent, or non-compliant use, the publisher may suspend or delete the account concerned, after assessing the facts. This is not a general content monitoring obligation.

s9.title: 9. Liability
s9.p1: Within limits allowed by law, the publisher is not liable for indirect damages, data loss due to an outage, your input errors, or non-compliant use of the service.
s9.p2: Nothing herein excludes liability that cannot be limited by law (including gross negligence or wilful misconduct, under applicable law).

delete.intro: This page explains how to delete a Pétanque Analytics account. It is accessible without an account, as required for Google Play. Deletion itself requires signing in so only the account holder can delete it.

s1.title: 1. How to delete your account
steps: Sign in with the email address of the account to delete.
Open this page, or go to Settings then Delete my account.
Confirm deletion in the confirmation dialog.

s2.title: 2. Data deleted
items: account creation date and email verification status;
email verification and password reset tokens;
session token validity: you are signed out and can no longer sign in with this email.

s3.title: 3. Data retained
s3.p1: The player profile (first name, last name, nickname) remains in the database, unlinked from any account. Matches, training and shooting sessions linked to that player are kept so shared history with other players is not erased. The link showing which account created a match is removed.
s3.p2: Drafts stored on the device are not sent to the server; signing out does not automatically clear those local drafts.

doc.title: Scoring Guide
doc.introduction: This guide explains the scoring scale used to rate every boule. The goal is to produce consistent and comparable statistics across all players.

why.title: Why rate boules?
why.text: The application does not judge a player's technical ability. It measures the actual impact of every boule on the end in order to generate meaningful statistics.

commonScale.title: A shared scoring scale
commonScale.text: For statistics to be meaningful, every player should use the same scale. With a little practice, rating boules becomes quick and natural.

minus2.title: 🟥 -2 · Harmful boule
minus2.description: The boule clearly makes the situation worse for your team.
minus2.example1: A point that pushes one of your own boules away.
minus2.example2: A missed shot that completely opens the game for the opponents.
minus2.example3: Any boule that causes your team to lose a significant advantage.
minus2.summary: A -2 boule clearly hurts your team.

minus1.title: 🟧 -1 · Useless boule
minus1.description: The boule brings no benefit to your team.
minus1.example2: A point far too long or too short.
minus1.example3: A boule that is completely out of play.
minus1.example4: A missed shot with no real consequence.
minus1.summary: The boule provides no useful contribution.

zero.title: ⚪ 0 · Average boule
zero.description: The boule has only a limited impact on the end.
zero.example1: A point that is fairly close but not good enough.
zero.example3: A boule that applies some pressure without really changing the game.
zero.summary: The boule has only a minor influence.

plus1.title: 🟩 +1 · Good boule
plus1.summary: A solid boule that does exactly what was expected.

plus2.title: 🟦 +2 · Outstanding boule
plus2.description: The boule gives your team a major advantage.
plus2.example3: A blocker that completely locks the game.
plus2.example4: Any boule that dramatically changes the outcome of the end.
plus2.summary: A +2 boule has a much greater impact than an ordinary good boule.

carreau.title: Is a carreau always worth +2?
carreau.answer: No. The rating always depends on the boule's actual impact. Most carreaux deserve +2, but a very easy or low-impact shot may simply be rated +1.

palet.title: Is a palet worth +2?
palet.answer: No. A palet is usually rated +1 because it perfectly achieves its objective. It only deserves +2 when it provides an exceptional advantage.

firstPoint.title: Can the first point of an end be worth +2?
firstPoint.answer: Yes. A first point that is almost impossible to beat or that immediately locks the end may deserve +2. A simply good first point remains +1.

difficulty.title: Is the difficulty of the throw taken into account?
difficulty.answer: No. The rating does not measure technical difficulty. It only measures the value the boule brings to the team when it is played.

beautiful.title: Can a technically beautiful boule receive a low rating?
beautiful.answer: Yes. A technically impressive boule with little real impact may receive an average rating. On the other hand, a less spectacular boule may deserve +2 if its impact is exceptional.

philosophy.title: The philosophy behind the system
philosophy.text1: A rating does not reward a beautiful throw. It only measures the value the boule brings to the team.
philosophy.text2: When everyone uses the same scale, statistics become comparable between players and across matches.
philosophy.quote: Don't ask yourself whether the boule was beautiful. Ask yourself how much it brought to your team.
